title: Improving cardiac magnetic resonance imaging with deep-learning image reconstruction in patients with cardiomyopathy
summary:
By means of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), images are generated that show the function and condition of the heart muscle: for example, scarring ("fibrosis") of the muscle, water retention ("oedema") or a functional restriction of the heart muscle. Oedema occurs, for example, in heart muscle inflammation or infarction. However, it is difficult to visualise oedema or scarring that is widespread throughout the heart muscle, and it is often impossible or insufficient to make a definite diagnosis. 
We have new methods for possibly performing cardiac imaging better than before: so-called "quantitative" methods, as well as new methods of computer-assisted image post-processing to reduce noise and image disturbances ("artefacts").

This study now aims to achieve the following goals: 
- The improved detection of diffuse, i.e. unclear or blurred, fibrosis, diffuse oedema or functional impairment of the heart.
- The detection of unintentional artefacts ("image errors") - with the aim of better recognising their occurrence and avoiding them in the future.
- To answer the question of how image artefacts influence the measurement results.

Our long-term goals are
- Improved imaging and diagnosis of the condition of the heart muscle, especially in patients with impaired heart function.
- Adjustments to the examination protocol that contribute to improving the image quality and, if necessary, to shortening the examination time while maintaining the same high image quality.

In order to achieve these goals, cardiac MRIs would first be performed in healthy individuals in order to make a preliminary selection among the new cardiac measurement methods to be tested. In cardiac patients, selected additional MRI (test) images will be generated within the framework of this study, but these may not yet be used for diagnosis. This prolongs the examination by about 10 minutes.
conditions: Complications and ill-defined descriptions of heart disease

interventions.name:
For healthy subjects:
A cardiac MRI without contrast agent.

For patients:
Patients receive a contrast-enhanced cardiac MRI due to a clinical indication.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For healthy subjects:
- Age ≥18 years,
- Written informed consent, including consent to report incidental findings.

For patients:
- Suspicion of cardiomyopathy and / or myocardial fibrosis,
- Clinical indication for cardiac MRI by treating cardiologist,
- Age ≥18 years,
- Written consent of the patient/ Legal guardians

Amendment 1: Inclusion of children under 18 years of age possible: Children or adolescent patients with congenital and acquired heart defects and indication for cardiac MRI
Exclusion criteria:
For healthy subjects:
- Subjects who are not capable of giving consent,
- Presence of non-MR-compatible implants or any kind of metal in and on the body (e.g. pacemakers, artificial heart valves, implanted magnetic metal parts, etc. that are not MR-compatible),
- Increased sensitivity to loud noises,
- Claustrophobia,
- Obesity with >150 kg body weight.

For patients:
- Presence of non-MR compatible implants or any type of metal in and on the body (e.g. pacemakers, artificial heart valves, implanted magnetic metal parts, etc. that are not MR compatible),
- Increased sensitivity to loud noises,
- Claustrophobia,
- Obesity with >150 kg body weight,
- Contraindication to MRI-contrast agent,
- Limited capacity to give consent.
